CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, skip this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. This is not optional. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## Instruction Priority

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

1. **User's explicit instructions** (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) — highest priority
2. **Superpowers skills** — override default system behavior where they conflict
3. **Default system prompt** — lowest priority

If CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or AGENTS.md says "don't use TDD" and a skill says "always use TDD," follow the user's instructions. The user is in control.

## How to Access Skills

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to you—follow it directly. Never use the Read tool on skill files.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins. The `skill` tool works the same as Claude Code's `Skill` tool.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

## Platform Adaptation

Skills use Claude Code tool names. Non-CC platforms: see `references/copilot-tools.md` (Copilot CLI), `references/codex-tools.md` (Codex) for tool equivalents. Gemini CLI users get the tool mapping loaded automatically via GEMINI.md.

# Using Skills

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

```dot
digraph skill_flow {
    "User message received" [shape=doublecircle];
    "About to EnterPlanMode?" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Already brainstormed?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" [shape=box];
    "Might any skill apply?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke Skill tool" [shape=box];
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" [shape=box];
    "Has checklist?" [shape=diamond];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [shape=box];
    "Follow skill exactly" [shape=box];
    "Respond (including clarifications)" [shape=doublecircle];

    "About to EnterPlanMode?" -> "Already brainstormed?";
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Invoke brainstorming skill" [label="no"];
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Might any skill apply?" [label="yes"];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" -> "Might any skill apply?";

    "User message received" -> "Might any skill apply?";
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Invoke Skill tool" [label="yes, even 1%"];
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Respond (including clarifications)" [label="definitely not"];
    "Invoke Skill tool" -> "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'";
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" -> "Has checklist?";
    "Has checklist?" -> "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [label="yes"];
    "Has checklist?" -> "Follow skill exactly" [label="no"];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" -> "Follow skill exactly";
}
```

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills could apply, use this order:

1. **Process skills first** (brainstorming, debugging) - these determine HOW to approach the task
2. **Implementation skills second** (frontend-design, mcp-builder) - these guide execution

"Let's build X" → brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
"Fix this bug" → debugging first, then domain-specific skills.

## Skill Types

**Rigid** (TDD, debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

**Flexible** (patterns): Adapt principles to context.

The skill itself tells you which.

## User Instructions

Instructions say WHAT, not HOW. "Add X" or "Fix Y" doesn't mean skip workflows.

    ## Security Guidance: Secure-by-Default Libraries

    When writing code, consider using these security-focused libraries that follow secure-by-default principles:

    ### Key Security Libraries by Category:

    **HTTP Security Headers**
    - Helmet.js (Node.js), secure_headers (Ruby) - Set protective HTTP response headers

    **XSS Prevention**
    - DOMPurify (JS), Bleach (Python), Ammonia (Rust) - Sanitize HTML safely

    **CSRF Protection**
    - Gorilla CSRF (Go), anti-csrf (PHP) - Token-based CSRF defense

    **Cryptography**
    - Google Tink (multi-language) - Secure, easy-to-use crypto APIs
    - Themis (14+ platforms) - High-level crypto framework

    **Input Validation**
    - Safe-regex - Detect catastrophic regex
    - defusedxml (Python) - Prevent XML attacks

    **SSRF Defense**
    - ssrf_filter (Ruby), ssrf-req-filter (Node.js) - Block private IP connections

    **Deserialization**
    - SerialKiller (Java) - Safe deserialization

    **Template Engines**
    - Mustache, Handlebars, Liquid - Logic-less templates prevent injection

    For detailed information, see: https://github.com/tldrsec/awesome-secure-defaults

**File:** `/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/web-backend/organize/web_views.py` (lines 195-217)

- Passes payload buckets ("overdue", "today", "this_week") to template

### The Filtering Logic

**File:** `/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/web-backend/organize/services.py` (lines 2097-2122)

The `get_dashboard_payload()` function applies filters for each section:

#### "Today" Section (lines 2097-2105):
```python
"today": tasks.filter(
    status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
).filter(
    Q(due_at__gte=today_start, due_at__lt=today_bucket_end)
    | Q(
        due_window_start_at__lt=today_bucket_end,
        due_window_end_at__gte=today_start,
    )
),
```
**Requirement:** Tasks appear in "Today" ONLY if:
- `due_at` is between today's start and end, **OR**
- Both `due_window_start_at` and `due_window_end_at` overlap with today

Tasks with **no due_at and no due_window dates** are completely filtered out.

#### "This Week" Section (lines 2106-2114):
```python
"this_week": tasks.filter(
    status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
).filter(
    Q(due_at__gte=today_bucket_end, due_at__lte=week_end)
    | Q(
        due_window_start_at__lte=week_end,
        due_window_end_at__gte=today_bucket_end,
    )
),
```
Same issue: requires either a `due_at` in the future week OR both window dates.

#### "Overdue" Section (lines 2115-2122):
```python
"overdue": tasks.filter(
    status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
)
.exclude(task_series__is_as_needed=True)
.filter(
    Q(due_window_end_at__lt=now)
    | Q(due_window_end_at__isnull=True, due_at__lt=now)
),
```
This one allows `due_window_end_at__isnull=True` IF `due_at < now` (past due), but excludes tasks with null dates in the future.

The API endpoint `/api/organize/dashboard/` in `organize/api.py` (lines 111-135) uses identical logic in `_apply_bucket_filter()`.

Let me now produce the final implementation plan. --- ## Implementation Plan: Unscheduled Tasks Bucket ### Problem Summary Tasks created without `due_at`, `due_window_start_at`, or `due_window_end_at` are invisible on the Tasks dashboard. All three display buckets (Overdue, Today, This Week) use date-based filters, so dateless tasks fall through. This was exposed by medication task creation where `_resolve_next_due_window` returns `(None, None, None)` when it cannot parse a time from the input. ### Design Decisions **1. As-needed (PRN) medication tasks belong in Unscheduled.** The overdue bucket explicitly excludes them (`.exclude(task_series__is_as_needed=True)`) because they cannot be "late." They naturally belong in Unscheduled since they have no dates. This means PRN medication tasks will persist in the Unscheduled bucket until marked as administered/completed. This is the correct UX -- they represent available-to-take medications and should remain visible. **2. The bucket should NOT exclude any task kinds.** Any PENDING task with all three date fields null should appear here, regardless of `task_kind` (MANUAL, CHORE, MEDICATION) or whether it has a `task_series`. The goal is: no invisible tasks. **3. Sort by newest first.** Since `due_at` is null for all tasks in this bucket, the default model ordering (`["status", "due_at", "created_at"]`) would be arbitrary. Use explicit `.order_by("-created_at")` so most recently created tasks surface first. **4. Mobile compatibility.** The mobile `BackendOrganizeDashboardSchema` uses `.passthrough()`, so adding a new key to the API response won't break validation. However, the mobile dashboard screen only merges `today + overdue` for its task preview. The `OrganizeTaskBoard` (the Tasks tab with filter chips) uses the `listTasks` API with bucket filtering. The `DUE_OPTIONS` array needs an "Unscheduled" option for full mobile parity. ### Implementation Steps #### Step 1: `organize/services.py` -- Add "unscheduled" to the payload dict In `get_dashboard_payload()` around line 2096, add: ```python "unscheduled": tasks.filter( status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING, due_at__isnull=True, due_window_start_at__isnull=True, due_window_end_at__isnull=True, ).order_by("-created_at"), ``` Place this after the "overdue" entry and before "today_events". The filter logic is simple: all three date fields must be null and status must be PENDING. #### Step 2: `organize/api.py` -- Add "unscheduled" to API response and bucket filter **A. Dashboard response** (`api.py` ~line 569-591): Add to `response_payload`: ```python "unscheduled": FamilyTaskSerializer( payload["unscheduled"], many=True, context={"request": request} ).data, ``` **B. Bucket filter** (`_apply_bucket_filter` ~line 105-135): Add a new condition: ```python if bucket == "unscheduled": return queryset.filter( due_at__isnull=True, due_window_start_at__isnull=True, due_window_end_at__isnull=True, ) ``` #### Step 3: `organize/web_views.py` -- Pass unscheduled to template context In `tasks_board()` (~line 210-216), add to the context dict: ```python "unscheduled_tasks": list(payload["unscheduled"]), ``` #### Step 4: `templates/organize/tasks_board.html` -- Add Unscheduled section Insert between "This Week" (line 169) and "Recently Completed" (line 173): ```html {# Unscheduled #} {% if unscheduled_tasks %}

Unscheduled

{{ unscheduled_tasks|length }}
{% for task in unscheduled_tasks %} {% include "organize/_task_row.html" with task=task %} {% endfor %}
{% endif %} ``` Note: The section is conditionally rendered (only shown when there are unscheduled tasks), matching the pattern of "Recently Completed". Use `bi-inbox` icon to convey "not yet placed on a timeline." #### Step 5: Mobile API type and filter chip updates **A.** `mobile/src/api/organize.ts` line 27: Update the type: ```typescript export type OrganizeTaskBucket = 'today' | 'this_week' | 'overdue' | 'unscheduled' | 'all'; ``` **B.** `mobile/src/components/organize/OrganizeTaskBoard.tsx` lines 47-52: Add to `DUE_OPTIONS`: ```typescript { value: 'unscheduled', label: 'Unscheduled' }, ``` **C.** `mobile/src/api/schemas/organize.schema.ts` line 449-461: Add to `BackendOrganizeDashboardSchema`: ```typescript unscheduled: z.array(FamilyTaskSchema).default([]), ``` **D.** `desktop/src/renderer/lib/useTasks.ts` line 17: Update the type: ```typescript export type TasksBucket = 'today' | 'this_week' | 'overdue' | 'unscheduled'; ``` #### Step 6: Tests Add to `organize/tests.py`: 1. **`test_dashboard_payload_includes_unscheduled`**: Create a PENDING task with all date fields null, call `get_dashboard_payload()`, assert the task appears in `payload["unscheduled"]`. 2. **`test_unscheduled_excludes_dated_tasks`**: Create a task with a `due_at`, verify it does NOT appear in `payload["unscheduled"]`. 3. **`test_bucket_filter_unscheduled`**: Hit `/api/organize/tasks/?bucket=unscheduled` and verify only dateless tasks are returned. 4. **`test_as_needed_medication_in_unscheduled`**: Create a PENDING task with `task_series__is_as_needed=True` and no dates, verify it appears in `unscheduled` (not filtered out). 5. **Update existing test** at line 219-232: Add `assert "unscheduled" in response.data`. ### Edge Cases | Case | Behavior | |------|----------| | As-needed PRN medication, no dates | Appears in Unscheduled (correct -- shows it's available) | | Manually created task, no dates | Appears in Unscheduled | | Task with `due_at` only | Appears in Today/This Week/Overdue (not Unscheduled) | | Task with `due_window_start_at` only (no `due_at`) | NOT unscheduled -- has scheduling info | | Completed task, no dates | NOT in Unscheduled (status filter ensures PENDING only) | | Task gains a date later (via edit) | Moves out of Unscheduled into appropriate date bucket | ### Cache Considerations The desktop response cache (`api.py:548-554`) caches the full response dict. Existing cached entries won't have the `unscheduled` key until natural invalidation. This is acceptable because: - Cache TTL is short-lived (per the "short_lived_desktop_cache" test name) - The key is additive -- old cached responses just won't have it - New requests after cache expiry will include it ### Critical Files for Implementation - `/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/web-backend/organize/services.py` - `/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/web-backend/organize/api.py` - `/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/web-backend/organize/web_views.py` - `/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/web-backend/templates/organize/tasks_board.html` - `/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/web-backend/organize/tests.py`

# Fix: Tasks without dates invisible on Tasks board

## Context

Medication task creation via Clancy created 4 tasks but only 1 appeared on the Tasks dashboard. The visible task had `due_at = May 23, 10:00 PM`; the other 3 had no date fields set (no `due_at`, no `due_window_start_at`, no `due_window_end_at`).

Root cause: all 3 dashboard buckets (Overdue, Today, This Week) require date fields in their query filters. Tasks with all dates null fall through every bucket and become invisible. This affects any task without dates — medication, manual, or chore.

## Approach: Add "Unscheduled" bucket

Add a 4th bucket for PENDING tasks where all date fields are null. Sorted by newest first.

### Backend changes (web-backend)

**1. `organize/services.py` — `get_dashboard_payload()` (~line 2096)**

Add to payload dict after "overdue":
```python
"unscheduled": tasks.filter(
    status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
    due_at__isnull=True,
    due_window_start_at__isnull=True,
    due_window_end_at__isnull=True,
).order_by("-created_at"),
```

**2. `organize/web_views.py` — `tasks_board()` (~line 210)**

Add to context: `"unscheduled_tasks": list(payload["unscheduled"])`

**3. `templates/organize/tasks_board.html`**

Insert between This Week and Recently Completed. Conditionally rendered (only when non-empty). Icon: `bi-inbox`.

**4. `organize/api.py`**

- `_apply_bucket_filter()`: add `bucket == "unscheduled"` case
- Dashboard response: serialize `payload["unscheduled"]` into response

### Mobile/Desktop (note for follow-up)

- `mobile/src/api/organize.ts` — add `'unscheduled'` to `OrganizeTaskBucket` type
- `mobile/src/components/organize/OrganizeTaskBoard.tsx` — add filter chip
- `mobile/src/api/schemas/organize.schema.ts` — add to dashboard schema
- `desktop/src/renderer/lib/useTasks.ts` — add to `TasksBucket` type

### Tests

- Task with no dates appears in `unscheduled`
- Task with `due_at` does NOT appear in `unscheduled`
- API `?bucket=unscheduled` returns only dateless tasks
- As-needed PRN medication (no dates) appears in `unscheduled`

## Verification

1. Run existing test suite: `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml exec web pytest organize/`
2. Create a medication bundle with mixed dated/undated tasks, verify all appear on board
3. Check web UI in browser — unscheduled section visible with correct tasks

def test_dashboard_groups_tasks_by_due_date(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        client = APIClient()
        client.force_authenticate(user=user)

        create_task_from_household_action(
            family=family,
            title="Schedule filter change",
            source_client_app="house",
            due_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=1),
        )
        create_task_from_household_action(
            family=family,
            title="Buy snacks",
            source_client_app="house",
            due_at=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=2),
        )
        local_now = timezone.localtime(timezone.now())
        today_noon = local_now.replace(hour=12, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
        Event.objects.create(
            title="School pickup",
            start_time=today_noon,
            end_time=today_noon + timedelta(hours=1),
            creator=user,
            family_group=family,
            visibility="PUBLIC",
        )
        client.post(
            "/api/organize/inbox-captures/",
            {
                "capture_type": "TEXT",
                "raw_text": "Send permission slip",
            },
            format="json",
            HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize",
        )

        response = client.get("/api/organize/dashboard/", HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize")

        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.data["client_app_context"]["client_app"] == "organize"
        assert len(response.data["overdue"]) == 1
        assert len(response.data["this_week"]) >= 1
        assert [item["title"] for item in response.data["today_events"]] == [
            "School pickup"
        ]
        assert "upcoming_events" in response.data
        assert "lists" in response.data
        assert "inbox" in response.data
        assert "grocery_lists" in response.data
        assert response.data["inbox"][0]["preview_text"] == "Send permission slip"

            family=family,
            title="Schedule filter change",

        with patch(

            first_response = client.get(

            second_response = client.get(
                "/api/organize/dashboard/",
                HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="desktop",
            )

        assert first_response.status_code == 200
        assert second_response.status_code == 200
        assert first_response.data == second_response.data

    def test_dashboard_returns_all_lists_with_types_and_counts(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        client = APIClient()
        client.force_authenticate(user=user)

        base_updated_at = timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=1)
        list_specs = [
            ("Groceries", "grocery", 2),
            ("Hardware", "hardware", 1),
            ("Pharmacy", "pharmacy", 3),
            ("General", "general", 0),
            ("Clothes", "clothes", 1),
            ("Weekend", "grocery", 4),
            ("Projects", "hardware", 2),
            ("Errands", "general", 1),
        ]

        expected_lists: list[dict[str, str | int]] = []
        for index, (name, list_type, item_count) in enumerate(list_specs, start=1):
            grocery_list = GroceryList.objects.create(
                family=family,
                owner=user,
                name=name,
                list_type=list_type,
            )
            GroceryList.objects.filter(pk=grocery_list.pk).update(
                updated_at=base_updated_at + timedelta(minutes=index)
            )
            grocery_list.refresh_from_db(fields=["updated_at"])

            for item_index in range(item_count):
                GroceryItem.objects.create(
                    grocery_list=grocery_list,
                    name=f"{name} item {item_index + 1}",
                    created_by=user,
                )

            expected_lists.insert(
                0,
                {
                    "id": str(grocery_list.id),
                    "name": name,
                    "list_type": list_type,
                    "item_count": item_count,
                },
            )

        response = client.get("/api/organize/dashboard/", HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize")

        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.data["grocery_lists"] == response.data["lists"]
        assert [
            {
                "id": item["id"],
                "name": item["name"],
                "list_type": item["list_type"],
                "item_count": item["item_count"],
            }
            for item in response.data["lists"]
        ] == expected_lists

    def test_dashboard_returns_all_lists_with_types_and_counts(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        client = APIClient()
        client.force_authenticate(user=user)

        base_updated_at = timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=1)
        list_specs = [
            ("Groceries", "grocery", 2),
            ("Hardware", "hardware", 1),
            ("Pharmacy", "pharmacy", 3),
            ("General", "general", 0),
            ("Clothes", "clothes", 1),
            ("Weekend", "grocery", 4),
            ("Projects", "hardware", 2),
            ("Errands", "general", 1),
        ]

        expected_lists: list[dict[str, str | int]] = []
        for index, (name, list_type, item_count) in enumerate(list_specs, start=1):
            grocery_list = GroceryList.objects.create(
                family=family,
                owner=user,
                name=name,
                list_type=list_type,
            )
            GroceryList.objects.filter(pk=grocery_list.pk).update(
                updated_at=base_updated_at + timedelta(minutes=index)
            )
            grocery_list.refresh_from_db(fields=["updated_at"])

            for item_index in range(item_count):
                GroceryItem.objects.create(
                    grocery_list=grocery_list,
                    name=f"{name} item {item_index + 1}",
                    created_by=user,
                )

            expected_lists.insert(
                0,
                {
                    "id": str(grocery_list.id),
                    "name": name,
                    "list_type": list_type,
                    "item_count": item_count,
                },
            )

        response = client.get("/api/organize/dashboard/", HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize")

                "name": item["name"],
                "list_type": item["list_type"],
                "item_count": item["item_count"],
            }
            for item in response.data["lists"]

class TestComputeNextDueAt:
    def test_none_returns_none(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.now()
        assert compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE) is None

    def test_daily_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))  # Sunday
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_weekly_advances_seven_days(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=7)

    def test_weekdays_friday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        friday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 20, 9, 0))
        assert friday.weekday() == 4
        result = compute_next_due_at(friday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sat, which rolls to Mon (+3 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == friday + timedelta(days=3)

    def test_weekdays_saturday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        saturday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 21, 9, 0))
        assert saturday.weekday() == 5
        result = compute_next_due_at(saturday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sun, which rolls to Mon (+2 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == saturday + timedelta(days=2)

    def test_weekdays_midweek_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        wednesday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 18, 9, 0))
        assert wednesday.weekday() == 2
        result = compute_next_due_at(wednesday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        assert result == wednesday + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_monthly_simple(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2026 is not a leap year -> Feb 28.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 2, 28, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february_leap_year(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2028 is a leap year -> Feb 29.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 2, 29, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_december_rolls_to_january(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 12, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2027, 1, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_none_due_at_anchors_on_now(self) -> None:
        result = compute_next_due_at(None, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result is not None
        # Should be roughly 1 day from now.
        delta = result - timezone.now()
        assert timedelta(hours=23) < delta < timedelta(hours=25)

        FamilyMembership.objects.create(

        )

        profile.save(update_fields=["primary_family"])
        family.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
        family.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
        return family, user

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_returns_none_for_non_recurring(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="One-off",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE,
        )
        assert spawn_next_occurrence(task) is None
        assert FamilyTask.objects.filter(family=family).count() == 1

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_inherits_fields_and_sets_parent(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        original_due = timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Water plants",
            notes="Use the watering can",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=original_due,
            assigned_to=user,
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY,
        )
        spawned = spawn_next_occurrence(task)
        assert spawned is not None
        assert spawned.title == "Water plants"
        assert spawned.notes == "Use the watering can"
        assert spawned.status == FamilyTask.Status.PENDING
        assert spawned.assigned_to_id == user.id
        assert spawned.recurrence == FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY
        assert spawned.recurrence_parent_id == task.id
        assert spawned.due_at == original_due + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_spawn_preserves_series_root_for_grandchild(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        root = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Trash",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY,
        )
        child = spawn_next_occurrence(root)
        assert child is not None
        grandchild = spawn_next_occurrence(child)
        assert grandchild is not None
        # Grandchild's parent should still point at the root, not the child.

            ("Hardware", "hardware", 1),
            ("Pharmacy", "pharmacy", 3),
            ("General", "general", 0),
            ("Clothes", "clothes", 1),
            ("Weekend", "grocery", 4),
            ("Projects", "hardware", 2),
            ("Errands", "general", 1),
        ]

        expected_lists: list[dict[str, str | int]] = []
        for index, (name, list_type, item_count) in enumerate(list_specs, start=1):
            grocery_list = GroceryList.objects.create(
                family=family,
                owner=user,
                name=name,
                list_type=list_type,
            )

                updated_at=base_updated_at + timedelta(minutes=index)
            )
            grocery_list.refresh_from_db(fields=["updated_at"])

            for item_index in range(item_count):
                GroceryItem.objects.create(
                    grocery_list=grocery_list,
                    name=f"{name} item {item_index + 1}",
                    created_by=user,
                )

            expected_lists.insert(
                0,

                    "name": name,
                    "list_type": list_type,
                    "item_count": item_count,
                },
            )

        assert response.data["grocery_lists"] == response.data["lists"]
        assert [
            {
                "id": item["id"],
                "name": item["name"],
                "list_type": item["list_type"],
                "item_count": item["item_count"],
            }

class TestComputeNextDueAt:
    def test_none_returns_none(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.now()
        assert compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE) is None

    def test_daily_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))  # Sunday
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_weekly_advances_seven_days(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=7)

    def test_weekdays_friday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        friday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 20, 9, 0))
        assert friday.weekday() == 4
        result = compute_next_due_at(friday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sat, which rolls to Mon (+3 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == friday + timedelta(days=3)

    def test_weekdays_saturday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        saturday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 21, 9, 0))
        assert saturday.weekday() == 5
        result = compute_next_due_at(saturday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sun, which rolls to Mon (+2 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == saturday + timedelta(days=2)

    def test_weekdays_midweek_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        wednesday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 18, 9, 0))
        assert wednesday.weekday() == 2
        result = compute_next_due_at(wednesday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        assert result == wednesday + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_monthly_simple(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2026 is not a leap year -> Feb 28.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 2, 28, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february_leap_year(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2028 is a leap year -> Feb 29.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 2, 29, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_december_rolls_to_january(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 12, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2027, 1, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_none_due_at_anchors_on_now(self) -> None:
        result = compute_next_due_at(None, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result is not None
        # Should be roughly 1 day from now.
        delta = result - timezone.now()
        assert timedelta(hours=23) < delta < timedelta(hours=25)

        FamilyMembership.objects.create(

        )
        profile = user.profile
        profile.primary_family = family
        profile.save(update_fields=["primary_family"])
        family.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
        family.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
        return family, user

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_returns_none_for_non_recurring(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="One-off",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE,
        )
        assert spawn_next_occurrence(task) is None
        assert FamilyTask.objects.filter(family=family).count() == 1

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_inherits_fields_and_sets_parent(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        original_due = timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Water plants",
            notes="Use the watering can",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=original_due,
            assigned_to=user,
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY,
        )
        spawned = spawn_next_occurrence(task)
        assert spawned is not None
        assert spawned.title == "Water plants"
        assert spawned.notes == "Use the watering can"
        assert spawned.status == FamilyTask.Status.PENDING
        assert spawned.assigned_to_id == user.id
        assert spawned.recurrence == FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY
        assert spawned.recurrence_parent_id == task.id
        assert spawned.due_at == original_due + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_spawn_preserves_series_root_for_grandchild(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        root = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Trash",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY,
        )
        child = spawn_next_occurrence(root)
        assert child is not None
        grandchild = spawn_next_occurrence(child)
        assert grandchild is not None
        # Grandchild's parent should still point at the root, not the child.
        assert grandchild.recurrence_parent_id == root.id

        assert [item["title"] for item in response.data["today_events"]] == [

        assert "upcoming_events" in response.data
        assert "lists" in response.data
        assert "inbox" in response.data
        assert "grocery_lists" in response.data

    def test_dashboard_today_events_include_display_member_for_external_calendar(

        family, user = self._setup_family()
        client = APIClient()
        client.force_authenticate(user=user)

            user=user,

    def test_dashboard_returns_all_lists_with_types_and_counts(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        client = APIClient()
        client.force_authenticate(user=user)

        base_updated_at = timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=1)
        list_specs = [
            ("Groceries", "grocery", 2),
            ("Hardware", "hardware", 1),
            ("Pharmacy", "pharmacy", 3),
            ("General", "general", 0),
            ("Clothes", "clothes", 1),
            ("Weekend", "grocery", 4),
            ("Projects", "hardware", 2),
            ("Errands", "general", 1),
        ]

        expected_lists: list[dict[str, str | int]] = []
        for index, (name, list_type, item_count) in enumerate(list_specs, start=1):
            grocery_list = GroceryList.objects.create(
                family=family,
                owner=user,
                name=name,
                list_type=list_type,
            )
            GroceryList.objects.filter(pk=grocery_list.pk).update(
                updated_at=base_updated_at + timedelta(minutes=index)
            )
            grocery_list.refresh_from_db(fields=["updated_at"])

            for item_index in range(item_count):
                GroceryItem.objects.create(
                    grocery_list=grocery_list,
                    name=f"{name} item {item_index + 1}",
                    created_by=user,
                )

            expected_lists.insert(
                0,
                {
                    "id": str(grocery_list.id),
                    "name": name,
                    "list_type": list_type,
                    "item_count": item_count,
                },
            )

        response = client.get("/api/organize/dashboard/", HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize")

        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.data["grocery_lists"] == response.data["lists"]
        assert [
            {
                "id": item["id"],
                "name": item["name"],
                "list_type": item["list_type"],
                "item_count": item["item_count"],
            }
            for item in response.data["lists"]
        ] == expected_lists

class TestComputeNextDueAt:
    def test_none_returns_none(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.now()
        assert compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE) is None

    def test_daily_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))  # Sunday
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_weekly_advances_seven_days(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=7)

    def test_weekdays_friday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        friday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 20, 9, 0))
        assert friday.weekday() == 4
        result = compute_next_due_at(friday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sat, which rolls to Mon (+3 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == friday + timedelta(days=3)

    def test_weekdays_saturday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        saturday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 21, 9, 0))
        assert saturday.weekday() == 5
        result = compute_next_due_at(saturday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sun, which rolls to Mon (+2 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == saturday + timedelta(days=2)

    def test_weekdays_midweek_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        wednesday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 18, 9, 0))
        assert wednesday.weekday() == 2
        result = compute_next_due_at(wednesday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        assert result == wednesday + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_monthly_simple(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2026 is not a leap year -> Feb 28.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 2, 28, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february_leap_year(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2028 is a leap year -> Feb 29.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 2, 29, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_december_rolls_to_january(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 12, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2027, 1, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_none_due_at_anchors_on_now(self) -> None:
        result = compute_next_due_at(None, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result is not None
        # Should be roughly 1 day from now.
        delta = result - timezone.now()
        assert timedelta(hours=23) < delta < timedelta(hours=25)

class TestRecurrenceSpawn:
    def _setup_family(self) -> Any:
        family = FamilyGroup.objects.create(name="Recurrence Family")
        user = User.objects.create_user(username="rec-user", password="pass")
        FamilyMembership.objects.create(
            user=user, family=family, role="PARENT", is_admin=True
        )
        profile = user.profile
        profile.primary_family = family
        profile.save(update_fields=["primary_family"])
        family.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
        family.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
        return family, user

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_returns_none_for_non_recurring(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="One-off",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE,
        )
        assert spawn_next_occurrence(task) is None
        assert FamilyTask.objects.filter(family=family).count() == 1

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_inherits_fields_and_sets_parent(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        original_due = timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Water plants",
            notes="Use the watering can",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=original_due,
            assigned_to=user,
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY,
        )
        spawned = spawn_next_occurrence(task)
        assert spawned is not None
        assert spawned.title == "Water plants"
        assert spawned.notes == "Use the watering can"
        assert spawned.status == FamilyTask.Status.PENDING
        assert spawned.assigned_to_id == user.id
        assert spawned.recurrence == FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY
        assert spawned.recurrence_parent_id == task.id
        assert spawned.due_at == original_due + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_spawn_preserves_series_root_for_grandchild(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        root = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Trash",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY,
        )
        child = spawn_next_occurrence(root)
        assert child is not None
        grandchild = spawn_next_occurrence(child)
        assert grandchild is not None
        # Grandchild's parent should still point at the root, not the child.
        assert grandchild.recurrence_parent_id == root.id
